Findings:  There is a mild knee effusion. There is a parrot beak tear of the posterior horn of the lateral meniscus with a fragment flipped posteroinferiorly. Normal medial meniscus.  Normal ACL, PCL, MCL and LCL. Normal extensor mechanism.  The tibiofemoral and patellofemoral articular cartilage is normal. Normal visualized bones and surrounding soft tissues.  
Conclusion: Posteroinferiorly flipped tear of the posterior horn of the lateral meniscus.

Findings: No evidence of knee effusion. Normal medial and lateral menisci. No evidence of tears.  Normal ACL, PCL, MCL and LCL. Normal extensor mechanism.  There is mild thinning of the medial compartment articular cartilage but no underlying bony change. The lateral compartment articular cartilage is well preserved. Mild patellofemoral articular cartilage thinning is also seen. Normal visualized bones and surrounding soft tissues.  
Conclusion: Mild degenerate changes as described.

Gonalgia izquierda.

No hay alteración de señal difusa la médula ósea.
Ligamentos cruzados y colaterales continuos.

meniscal, quiste parameniscal de 7 x 6 mm y edema de las partes blandas para meniscales.

prominencias osteofíticas marginales.
Cartílago patelofemoral de espesor y señal conservados sin defectos condrales profundos.

quiste parameniscal y edema de partes blandas para meniscales.

Moderado derrame articular con signos de sinovitis difusa.
Quiste poplíteo con signos de leve filtración

Aumento de señal central del cuerno posterior y parte del cuerpo del menisco medial de
predominio periférico, sugiriendo una rotura, no desplazada.
El menisco lateral impresiona presentar una rotura vertical periférica de su cuerno posterior, sin
desplazamiento de segmentos.
Cartílagos los compartimentos femorotibiales y patelofemoral sin alteraciones significativas.
Aumento de señal del aspecto superoexterno de la grasa de Hoffa.

Tendones de la pata de ganso, bíceps femoral y banda iliotibial dentro de límites normales.

Signos de una rotura periférica del menisco medial, no desplazada.
Rotura vertical periférica del cuerno posterior del menisco lateral, no desplazada.
Discretos signos de un síndrome de hiperpresión externa de rótula.
Tendinosis rotuliana proximal con rotura parcial y extensión hacia la aponeurosis prepatelar con
cambios óseos reparativos regionales.
Leve tendinosis cuadricipital dista

МР находка: МР  данни за ставен излив – наличие на течност в ретропателарната бурса. Костите, формиращи дясната колянна става са с нормална форма и структура. Ставният хрущял на тибията и фемура е със запазена конгруентност. Дорзално в медиалния кондил на тибията и в по- слаба степен от вътрешната страна на медиалния кондил на фемура се изобразяват зони а костномозъчен едем с повишен сигнален интензитет. МР данни за лезия на задния рог на медиалния менискус. Същата е задебелена, с кос ход и с хиперинтензитет на сигнала, като достига до артикулиращия хрущял на тибията. Увредата съответства на руптура 3-та степен.  Нормално изобразяване на двата рога на латералния менискус. Кръстни връзки – б.о.  Колатерални лигаменти - б.о. Ретинакулуми – б.о. Патела, хрущял на пателата – б.о. Малка предходно руптурирала Бекерова киста от медиалната страната на коляното. Нормално изобразяване на скенирните мускулни групи и меки тъкани. Заключение: Наличие на ставен излив. МР данни за лезия на задния рог на медиалния менискус – grade 3. Предходно руптурирала малка Бекерова киста.

MRI  KNEE  -  RIGHT

TECHNIQUE:  Unenhanced multiplanar multisequence MR images of the knee.

CLINICAL INDICATION:  Progressive right knee pain. Prior external ultrasound report details "unexplained knee joint effusion, recommend further evaluation with MRI to assess this sclerotic distal femoral lesion and for any possible internal derangement".

COMPARISON:  No prior imaging

FINDINGS:

Medial meniscus:  Intact.

Medial compartment articular cartilage:  Severe thinning of the articular cartilage of the medial tibiofemoral joint.

MCL:  Intact.

Lateral meniscus:  Intact.

Lateral compartment articular cartilage:  Mild thinning of the cartilage of the lateral tibiofemoral joint. There is slight concavity and cartilaginous thinning along the weightbearing aspect of the lateral femur, may be in keeping with an old osteochondral injury.

LCL complex:  Intact.

ACL:  Intact.

PCL:  Intact.

Quadriceps and patellar tendons:  Intact.

Patellofemoral alignment:  Normal 

Patellofemoral cartilage:  Severe chondrosis of the medial trochlea. Moderate cartilage thinning of the patella. No bony edema.

Joint effusion:  Small

Intra-articular bodies:  None.

Bone marrow:  Normal.

Popliteal fossa:  Normal.

Other findings:  Partially imaged distal femur. There is a T1 hypointense possibly expansile lesion partially visualized.


INTERPRETATION:

Mild-to-moderate degenerative changes of the medial compartment. Moderate to severe degenerative changes of the patellofemoral compartment.

The femur is not completely visualized on this knee MRI. There is a distal femur lesion, minimally visualized. Dedicated CT or MRI of the femur are recommended to further characterize this lesion.

MRI  KNEE  -  LEFT

TECHNIQUE:  Unenhanced multiplanar multisequence MR images of the knee.

CLINICAL INDICATION:  Left knee pain.

COMPARISON:  Correlated with knee radiograph dated [Date].

FINDINGS:

Nondiagnostic scout images were reviewed.

There is a tear involving the posterior root of the medial meniscus, characterized by disruption at its root attachment adjacent to the tibial plateau.

Extensive intrasubstance degeneration of the anterior and posterior horn of the lateral meniscus. No evidence of discrete tear.

ACL, PCL, MCL and LCL are intact.

Scattered area of chondrosis cartilaginous irregularities more prominent at the patellofemoral and medial tibiofemoral compartment.

Small volume joint effusion.

Benign cystic changes at the tibial spine/tibial eminence.

The extensor mechanism is intact, the quadriceps tendon and patellar tendon are unremarkable.

No bone marrow edema.

2.6 x 2.5 x 6.7 cm Baker's cyst.


INTERPRETATION:

Posterior root tear of the medial meniscus.

Extensive intrasubstance degeneration of the lateral meniscus without evidence of tear.

Scattered area of chondrosis with no evidence of fissuring or full thickness cartilage loss. Findings in keeping with mild OA.

Incidental finding of 6.7 cm Baker's cyst.

Impression:  

1. Fracture involving the posterior and anterior horns of the medial meniscus.

2. Microtrabecular insufficiency fracture involving the weightbearing aspect of the medial femoral condyle and probably the medial tibial plateau, with surrounding marrow edema as well as medial compartment osteoarthritis.

3. Marrow contusions involving the anterior aspect of the medial and lateral tibial plateau.


Technique:  Magnetic Resonance Imaging of the right knee was performed utilizing sagittal T2 weighted and fat suppressed proton density, coronal T1 weighted and fat suppressed proton density, and axial fat suppressed T2 weighted sequences.


Comment:

Menisci: The lateral meniscus is intact. There is a complex fracture involving the posterior horn of the medial meniscus, with extrusion of the meniscal body. There is also a horizontal fracture involving the anterior horn of the medial meniscus.

Cruciate ligaments: Intact

Collateral ligaments: Intact

Extensor mechanism: Quadriceps and patellar tendons are intact.

Joint fluid/Baker's cyst: There is a small to moderate joint effusion. There is also a moderate complex Baker's cyst which appears partially ruptured.

Bone marrow: A small crescentic focus of signal abnormality is noted in the subchondral weightbearing aspect of the medial femoral condyle, compatible with a microtrabecular insufficiency fracture with surrounding marrow edema. There is slight flattening of the articular surface at the site of the fracture. An additional small microtrabecular insufficiency fracture is suspected in the medial tibial plateau. There is also marrow edema along the anterior aspect of the medial and lateral tibial plateau suggesting marrow contusions.

Femorotibial joints: There is cartilage thinning involving the weightbearing aspect of the medial compartment, with joint space narrowing and osteophyte formation compatible with osteoarthritis. Mild cartilage thinning and heterogeneity are noted in the weightbearing aspect of the lateral compartment.

Patellofemoral joint: There is mild cartilage heterogeneity along the posterior patella.

Findings:  There is a minor knee effusion. Normal medial and lateral menisci. No evidence of tears.  Normal ACL, PCL, MCL and LCL. Normal extensor mechanism.  The tibiofemoral and patellofemoral articular cartilage is normal. Normal visualized bones and surrounding soft tissues.  
Conclusion: No significant abnormality identified.

> No evidence of bone contusion is noted.
> Subcutaneous edmea over right knee.
> Some varicose veins.

Impression: 
1. Osteoarthritis of right knee, more prominent at medial compartment with grade 4 chondromalacia.
2. Synovitis of right knee with suprapatellar bursitis and patellar plicae; R/O Lipoma arborescens.
3. Baker's cyst with perifocal edmea.
4. Tear of posterior horn of medial meniscus.
5. Subcutaneous edmea over right knee and some varicose veins.
6. Grade 1 injury of ACL.

SOL DİZ MRG. Tetkik protokolü: Çok düzlemli, çok sekanslı. Bulgular: Medial menisküste diz eklem mesafesinden 4 mm mediale ekstrüdedir. Menisküs hacminde azalma, posterior horn ve gövde kesiminde grade III dejenerasyon izlenmiştir. Lateral ve medial kollateral ligamanda grade I sprain izlenmiştir. Anterior çapraz bağda miksoid dejenerasyona sekonder sinyal değişikliği izlenmiştir. Tibia interkondiler eminens posteriorunda posterior çapraz bağ yapışma düzeyinde 1 cm çaplı subkondral kist izlenmiştir .Suprapatellar bursa ve diz eklem mesafesinde sıvı artışı izlenmiştir. Tibiofemoral eklem medialinde, eklem aralığında daralma, ekleme komşu kemik yüzlerde subkondral hafif kemik iliği ödemi izlendi. Femur medial kondilde ise 7x4 mm boyutlu fokal osteokondral defekt izlenmektedir. Bu düzeyde femoral ve tibial kartilajlarda incelme izlenmiştir. SONUÇ: gonartroz, medial menisküste hafif mediale ekstrüzyon ve grade III meniskopati, lateral menisküste grade II meniskopati, anterior çapraz bağda miksoid dejenerasyon, tibia interkondiler eminenste subkondral kist, suprpatellar bursit, diz ekleminde sinovit, medial kollateral ligamanda grade I sprain.

FINDINGS:

Fluid:
Mild to moderate joint effusion with a small popliteal cyst measuring 1.3 x 1.0 x 4.3 mm. There are no signs of leakage.

Medial compartment (meniscus, collateral ligament, cartilage):
The medial meniscus and the cartilage surfaces are unremarkable.
Mild edema of the meniscocapsular junction without fluid cleft.
High grade, almost complete tear of the superficial and anterior deep fibers of the femoral insertion of the medial collateral ligament with faint possible remaining attachment of the posterior deep fibers and the distal insertion.
There is periligamentous and pericapsular edema.
Medial suprapatellar plica as a variant.

Lateral compartment (meniscus, collateral ligament complex, cartilage):
The lateral meniscus and the lateral cartilage surfaces are unremarkable.
High-grade partial tear of the mid fibers of the lateral collateral ligament without retraction or complete discontinuity, although distal fibers are not clearly seen.
The remaining components of the lateral collateral complex are preserved.
Mild tendinopathy of the popliteus tendon and edema of the myotendinous junction a small synovial cyst.

Intercondylar compartment (anterior and posterior cruciate ligaments):
Complete discontinuity of the proximal fibers of the anterior cruciate ligament with reactive synovitis of the intercondylar notch. Mild associated anterior tibial translation.
The posterior cruciate ligament has a buckled appearance without tear.

Anterior compartment (extensor mechanism, cartilage, Hoffa's fat pad):
The extensor mechanism is unremarkable.
The patellofemoral cartilage is preserved.
Superficial soft tissue swelling a laminar fluid collection.

Bones:
Posterior lateral bone contusion without fracture line..

Muscles and neurovascular structures:
Subcutaneous soft tissue swelling and myotendinous junction tear of the fibers of the distal vastus lateralis.
Neurovascular bundles are unremarkable.

Other findings:
None

CONCLUSION:
1.Full-thickness tear of the proximal fibers of the anterior cruciate ligament
2.High-grade / almost complete tear of the superficial and deep components of the medial collateral ligament as detailed above.
3.High grade tear of the lateral collateral ligament.
4.Joint effusion and popliteal cyst.

For further findings, please see the body of the report.

Medyal menisküs arka boynuzu-gövdesindeki dejenerasyona yırtık eşlik etmiyor. Medyal menisküs arka kökü ödemli/mukoid dejenerasyon gösteriyor. Lateral menisküs normal. Medyal femoral tibyal ve patellofemoral eklem osteoartritleri femoral kondilin ağırlık taşıyan kesimindeki geniş tam kat kıkırdak kaybı ve eşlik eden subkortikal meduller fibrovasküler-fibrokistik değişiklikler ile karakterize. OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. Multiple areas of curvilinear serpiginous high T2 and low T1 signal intensity are noted in the distal femoral metadiaphysis as well as in the medial femoral condyle and proximal medial tibia with central areas of fat, characteristic for osteonecrosis. The largest in the femur measures up to 4.8 cm mediolateral by 2.5 cm anterior posterior by 7.1 cm craniocaudal dimension, with a thick peripheral rim of enhancement and central areas of fat signal intensity. These findings are age-indeterminate with a probable chronic component given the central fat and absence of surrounding geographic marrow edema. Very subtle periarticular edema is noted along the anteromedial aspect anterolateral aspect of the femoral condyles. There is mild nonspecific marrow edema and a patella. Mild marrow edema is noted at the anterior patella and deep to the popliteus tendon. No aggressive osseous lesions.

JOINT SPACE:
Minimal joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. No Baker's cyst.

Medial meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
